newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's PUMA bonds priced at 16.6 bp over.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's PUMA bonds priced at 16.6 bp over.

text.p: Macquarie Bank's securitisation arm, PUMA Management Ltd, said its P-6 Series A A$500 million four tranche mortgage backed bonds were priced at 16.6 basis points over the 90-day bank bill swap rate (BBSW).

The pricing was based on the weighted average margin overtime (WAMOT) over BBSW for the whole issue and compares with a spread of 21.3 basis points over for the P-5 Series B issue priced in September 1996.
PUMA Managing Director Tony Gill said the bonds were keenly sought by investors and PUMA achieved a further reduction in pricing with margins contracting across all four margins.

The A$315 million fixed rate Tranche 1-F, maturing April 15, 2000, was priced at 31 basis points over the benchmark Commonwealth Government 7.0 percent April 2000 bond, giving a coupon of 6.9 percent.
The other three tranches were floating rate transactions.

The A$135 million tranche two issue, which has an average expected life of 7.1 years, was priced at 19 basis points over BBSW, while the A$25 million tranche three issue with an average expected life of 7.6 years was priced at 21 basis points.
The A$25 million tranche four issue, which is subordinated debt, was priced at 37 basis points over BBSW.
"We are very pleased with the pricing of this issue which has set a new benchmark for PUMA," Gill said.

"Pricing on all four tranches was at the low end of our expected ranges. The pricing of our subordinated debt has contracted substantially, from 125 basis points over BBSW in December 1994 to 37 basis points over BSSW today," he said.

He added that the domestic market continues to support PUMA debt, which is highly rated -- AAA/Aaa by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service for tranches one to three -- and liquid stock, and that it was the benchmark in the Australian mortgage backed bond market.
The subordinated tranche 4 issue is rated AA minus by S&P.
